stem: A maturity check mixes observations from sugar leaves, bracts, and damaged tissue into one trichome-color percentage. Why is that method weak?
choices: Pooling unlike tissues can obscure meaningful developmental differences; comparable floral tissues should be sampled consistently
Any visible trichome has identical developmental significance regardless of tissue
Damaged tissue is always the best maturity reference
rationale: A defensible maturity assessment uses comparable, representative tissues and a consistent sampling method. Combining unlike or damaged tissues can make the resulting percentage difficult to interpret.
